documents.doc-cz-szu-2026-08-25-szu-10724-2026: The National Institute of Public Health responded to the information request concerning transport, storage and handover of human blood samples. It stated that pre-analytical handling and transport are the responsibility of the healthcare provider sending the sample, referred to its laboratory sampling manual, and stated that since 1 January 2021 it has recorded no degradation, refusal or challenge of a blood sample because of transport conditions.
documents.doc-cz-szu-2026-08-26-szu-10724-2026-dec: The National Institute of Public Health issued a decision partially refusing the information request under Section 11b of the Czech Freedom of Information Act. It refused information concerning methodologies, temperature ranges, transport without a validated box, high-temperature transport conditions, temperature monitoring and generally applicable validation requirements, stating that these matters fall within the competence of the healthcare providers sending samples. The decision may be appealed within 15 days to the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection through the Institute.
documents.doc-cz-msz-pha-2026-08-27-3-kzn-974-2026: The Prague Municipal Public Prosecutor’s Office completed supervisory review of the Prague 4 District Public Prosecutor’s Office in file 1 ZN 320/2026. It found no error requiring corrective action, dismissed the supervisory submission as unfounded and stated that the matter was finally disposed of at that level. It also advised that further submissions of identical content would no longer be reviewed or acknowledged.
